criteria_quotes: Total ankle replacement using an FDA approved device may be considered MEDICALLY NECESSARY in skeletally mature patients with moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity
Arthritis in adjacent joints (i.e., subtalar or midfoot); OR
Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle; OR
Arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle; OR
In general, patients selected for arthroplasty would not be good candidates for arthrodesis due to the presence of bilateral or subtalar arthritis or Chopart arthrosis.
Optimal candidates for total ankle replacement are considered to be older (age > 50), thin, low-demand individuals with minimal deformity.
Patients should have no funcitonal barriers to participation in a rehabilitation program.
Ankle arthroplasty should be performed by surgeons who are adequately trained and experienced in the specific techniques and devices used
answer.submission_route: Send a written request with your name, ID number, patient name and claim number to the address in your EOB's appeal-rights section. If filing for someone else, include their Designation of Authorized Representative form. Online: My Health Toolkit (to check claims; the appeal itself must be in writing) By mail: The mailing address listed in the appeal rights section of your EOB — they publish no single address By phone: The Customer Service number on the front page of your EOB Deadline: 180 days from the date on your EOB -- but your denial letter is authoritative.
